goal: Build a versioned reviewer eval corpus from committed audit records: eligible historical review cases with revision identity, finding anchor and evidence, acceptance text, and disposition, where resolved counts only as a silver label, gold labels are human-confirmed, clean cases are included, and the newest cases form a holdout validation split.

acceptance.assertion: Meet S0 in docs/specs/review-verifier-eval.spec.md: an offline extractor run at a pinned commit yields a deterministic corpus (same input commit produces byte-identical corpus.jsonl); a case enters the gold pool only when its finding is review-sourced with non-null evidence and anchor, its review_round is present, its review revision identity is recoverable, and both git objects are reachable, and ineligible records are excluded with counts by reason; the corpus validates against its schema and separates disposition (silver label) from gold (confirmed_true / confirmed_false / unlabeled) as distinct fields; the README states in its first paragraph that resolved is a silver label only and documents the gold labelling protocol (first set: 30 cases labelled by Derek, at least 10 confirmed_false or clean); at least 10 clean revisions from done tasks with no request_rework are included; the split is by task recency with the newest 20 percent held out as the validation split and is stable across regeneration. Selection of the 30 gold cases is uncertainty-first under an offline Jev-style pre-screen (scripts/review-eval/prescreen.ts) scoring every extracted finding likely_true, likely_false, or uncertain from its trigger, caller_chain, and violated fields: least-confident cases and cases whose lean disagrees with the silver disposition are labelled first, the classifier output is recorded only in a selection log with probabilities and reasons and never becomes a label or corpus gold, and disabling the pre-screen reproduces the weight-rule selection exactly.
